method: I selected two key terms from the reading: "crip technoscience" and "access aesthetics." I searched for their definitions in the original academic sources and verified the links. I then chose two artists mentioned in the introduction—Laura Forlano and Darrin Martin—and found one representative work for each, using gallery press releases and exhibition catalogues to describe them.
related_work: I draw on Chang and Felt's introduction, Hamraie and Fritsch's Crip Technoscience Manifesto, Cachia's The Agency of Access, and gallery materials on Forlano and Martin. These sources give the definitions and artwork details used below.
references:
[1] Chang, V., and Felt, L. D. 2024. Criptech and the Art of Access: Introduction to Special Issue. Leonardo 57, 2: 129–131. https://leonardo.info/journal-issue/leonardo/57/2
[2] Hamraie, A., and Fritsch, K. 2019. Crip Technoscience Manifesto. Catalyst: Feminism, Theory, Technoscience 5, 1: 1–33. https://catalystjournal.org/index.php/catalyst/article/view/29607
[3] Cachia, A. 2025. The Agency of Access: Contemporary Disability Art & Institutional Critique. Philadelphia: Temple University Press.
[4] Smack Mellon. 2023. "Itziar Barrio, did not feel low, was sleeping" press release. https://www.smackmellon.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/IB_PR.pdf
[5] Gallery 400. 2022. "Crip*" exhibition checklist. University of Illinois at Chicago. https://stage.gallery400.uic.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Crip_-Extended-Exhibiton-Checklist.docx
[6] Northeastern University. 2023. "Disability studies research incorporated into robotic sculpture." https://news.northeastern.edu/research/archives/forlanos-research-included-in-robotic-sculpture/
conclusion_future_work: My working answer is that crip technoscience provides the theoretical grounding (disabled people as experts and designers) while access aesthetics provides the creative method (translation, sensory expansion, touch, movement). Together they explain how criptech artists turn access from a functional requirement into a creative medium. In my own practice, I will pay more attention to how sensory translation can be built into digital art from the start rather than added afterwards.
results_discussion:
Term 1: Crip Technoscience. Hamraie and Fritsch define crip technoscience as a field at the intersection of feminist technoscience studies and critical disability studies, emphasising difference and embodiment at the core of disability politics. It recognises disabled people as "experts and designers of everyday life" and treats "crip" as a valued identity and site of embodied knowledge. The manifesto is published in Catalyst: Feminism, Theory, Technoscience, 5(1), April 2019.

Term 2: Access Aesthetics. Amanda Cachia coins "access aesthetics" in her 2025 book from Temple University Press. She argues that contemporary disabled artists create an art of access through works that centre translation, sensory expansion, touch, and movement, offering audiences an experience of "being with" disability rather than simply viewing it. Cachia identifies five key traits: translation, sensory aesthetics, movement, tactility, and exhibition design.

Artist 1: Laura Forlano. Forlano is a professor of art and design at Northeastern University and a Type 1 diabetic. Her collaboration with artist Itziar Barrio produced the exhibition "did not feel low, was sleeping" at Smack Mellon in Brooklyn (11 March–23 April 2023). The work consists of robotic sculptures programmed and inscribed with text that Forlano transcribed from the alert history of her "smart" insulin pump and annotated with field notes. The exhibition title comes directly from one of the sculptures. As CripTech art, the sculptures complicate discourses on AI and design by engaging themes of data as labour, data as material, and data as relations, ultimately arguing that both people and technologies are disabled.

Artist 2: Darrin Martin. Martin is an artist and professor at UC Davis who works with video, sound, sculpture, and print-based installations. His work Contrapposto (2016) is a 16-minute HD video paired with a 3D-printed sculpture. The piece fractures and reassembles a gay, male body through technological means, generating questions about identity and how it is produced. Martin, who has a cochlear implant, materialises the intricate boundaries present within his own experience of disability and technology. This work connects to crip technoscience because Martin uses technological means—3D scanning and video—to reconfigure the disabled body rather than simply represent it.

introduction: This week I read the introduction to the Leonardo special issue "Criptech and the Art of Access." I am asked to Choose 2-3 terms / words that I am not familiar with and explain them. I also need to select 1-2 artists and describe them.
